verdict.rationale: mParticle documents routing data to 'hundreds of vendors' through an integrations Directory, and community users confirm forwarding to around 10 analytics providers. Filtering is evidenced by forwarding rules, but the documented example is consent-specific. Per-destination mapping is evidenced only by a doc title about transforming data as it leaves mParticle. missing for 10: explicit docs for per-destination field/event mapping, general (non-consent) per-destination event and attribute filtering, and detailed documentation of the destination catalog's size and depth.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can route events to a large catalog of documented destination integrations with per-destination mapping and filtering

citations.quote: simplifies how you collect and connect your user data to hundreds of vendors without needing to manage multiple integrations
Navigate to Data Platform > Setup > Directory, and click the card for your audience partner of choice.
Applying a forwarding rule of: Do not forward if CCPA Data sale opt out is present.
Transform data as it enters and leaves mParticle
Now we have mParticle, so we can send data only to mParticle and then send it onwards to possibly 10 other analytics providers
